title: Leave what makes you doubt
cue: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not
arabic: عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ سِبْطِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَرَيْحَانَتِهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: حَفِظْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «دَعْ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَى مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ».
translation: It is narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, grandson of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his fragrant flower, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.”

gradings.in: al-Jami', after hadith 2518, in his words "hasan sahih" (quoted by al-Nawawi in the Forty)

witnesses.name: ibn-daqiq-sharh
witnesses.ref: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in, Mu'assasat al-Rayyan 2003, hadith 11, p. 61: https://shamela.ws/book/11244/51

witnesses.name: haytami-fath-al-mubin
witnesses.ref: al-Haytami, al-Fath al-Mubin, Dar al-Minhaj 2008, hadith 11, p. 293: https://shamela.ws/book/8889/289

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. Ibn Daqiq and hadith-api agree with ours. al-Haytami's print puts رضي الله عنهما before سبط; ours follows the other two. We vowel يَرِيبُك with fath on the ya, which Ibn Daqiq calls the more eloquent and better known reading; hadith-api has يُرِيبُك.

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id explains: leave what you are unsure of and turn to what you are not unsure of; he links it to [[hadith]] 6 on the unclear matters.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya
